item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00499","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C04","C20","C06"],"selected_candidate_label":"C04","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C04 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both are presidential letters to the U.S. representative entering a Geneva disarmament conference, and they follow the same distinctive sequence: describe the conference as a grave responsibility to mankind, caution against discouragement or expectations of easy progress, emphasize phased and safeguarded disarmament, charge the representative to exert every effort toward agreement, ask him to convey the President's hopes to the assembled delegates, and close by pledging presidential and public support. C20 and C06 share some disarmament language and motifs, but neither matches this combined occasion, audience, and operative structure as closely.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"As you and your colleagues from every quarter of the globe enter upon the work of the Geneva Disarmament Conference... the hopes and indeed the very prospects of mankind are involved","parent_excerpt":"The ten nations which will begin disarmament discussions at Geneva... have both the opportunity and a great responsibility to serve mankind.","explanation":"Both openings frame an imminent Geneva disarmament conference as a momentous responsibility affecting all humanity."},{"child_excerpt":"This task... is not a quick or easy one. It must be approached both boldly and responsibly... We must not be discouraged by initial disagreements","parent_excerpt":"We must not be pessimistic because of the lack of success in past disarmament negotiations. Nor should we necessarily expect immediate, dramatic and far-reaching strides","explanation":"The same rhetorical move tempers urgency with realism and directs persistence despite slow or disappointing negotiations."},{"child_excerpt":"The objective should be to define in treaty terms the widest area of agreement that can be implemented at the earliest possible time... initial measures of disarmament... agreement on a safeguarded nuclear test ban.","parent_excerpt":"it should be our objective in these negotiations to contribute by carefully balanced, phased and safeguarded arms control agreements","explanation":"Both identify safeguarded, implementable steps as the practical route toward broader disarmament."},{"child_excerpt":"It is your task as representative of the United States to join with your colleagues in a supreme effort toward that end.","parent_excerpt":"As the United States Representative... I know that you will exert every possible effort to reach agreement","explanation":"The operative charge to the U.S. representative is materially parallel."},{"child_excerpt":"Please convey... to the representatives of the nations assembled, our deep and abiding support... I pledge anew my personal and continuing interest in this work.","parent_excerpt":"I should like you to convey to the other delegates... my earnest hope... You may be assured that you carry with you my complete support and that of the people of the United States.","explanation":"The closings use nearly the same two-part machinery: convey the President's message to the delegates and affirm the support of both President and American people."}]}
